citations.narrative:
The facility was not sanitizing the guinea pig primary enclosures at least once every two weeks. The facility representative
stated that the enclosures were cleaned weekly, and the enclosures appeared sufficiently clean during the inspection.
However, sanitization was not being performed at the required minimum frequency.
Cleaning removes excreta and debris, while sanitization reduces disease hazards. Failure to sanitize primary enclosures
at least once every two weeks increases the risk of exposure to disease-causing organisms, even when the enclosures
appear clean.
The licensee must sanitize the guinea pig primary enclosures using a method provided in § 3.31(a)(4) and establish and
maintain a sanitization frequency of at least once every two weeks, or more often as necessary to prevent an
accumulation of excreta or debris.
To be corrected by: November 15, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
